name: Deity yoga (generation-stage sādhana)
method_summary: After refuge, bodhicitta and the protection circle, the practitioner dissolves ordinary appearance into emptiness, generates the maṇḍala and himself as the deity from seed syllables on sun and moon discs, invites the gnosis beings to merge with the visualized pledge beings, receives consecration and the seal of the family lord, maintains the deity's clarity and pride while reciting mantra, and finally dissolves and re-arises for activity.
signs_of_progress: stable clarity of the deity and the maṇḍala
readiness for the completion stage ('the staircase', Pañcakrama 1.2)

warnings.text: There is no meditator and nothing meditated, no mantra and no deity: they abide in the nature free of elaboration — the deity is not to be reified.
Saraha criticizes those who meditate on maṇḍala circles without the innate (People Dohā v10–13).

name: The five manifest awakenings
method_summary: Yoga-tantra generation: penetrating one's own mind (OṂ cittaprativedhaṃ karomi), generating bodhicitta as a moon disc, visualizing a vajra on it, making it firm (OṂ vajrātmako 'ham), and arising as the Buddha body (OṂ yathā sarvatathāgatās tathāham), modelled on Sarvārthasiddhi's awakening.

name: Vajra recitation (vajrajāpa)
method_summary: Joining the three syllables OṂ ĀḤ HŪṂ with the natural movement of the wind (entering, abiding, leaving), after recognizing the wind's five-coloured nature at the nose tip; the first stage (speech isolation) of the Pañcakrama.

warnings.text: This reality is sealed in the Samāja and must be understood through the explanatory tantras and the guru's mouth.

name: Meditation on the drop at the nose tip
method_summary: Visualizing a tiny drop or mustard seed (a five-coloured jewel) at the tip of the nose and resting the mind on it until the object dissolves into emptiness (Ajogi; Pañcakrama 1.10–11).
signs_of_progress: the mustard-seed object is lost in emptiness (Ajogi's song)

name: Inner heat (caṇḍālī)
method_summary: Summary only: meditation on the navel fire (caṇḍālī) in the central channel that melts the drop at the crown, giving rise to the four joys; taught in the Hevajra and first of Tilopa's six dharmas (from Caryāpa), with physical exercises. No method details are recorded here.

warnings.text: To be received only from the guru after consecration; revealing it to the unripe is a root downfall.
Saraha mocks those who force the winds and 'call themselves yogins out of pride' (King Dohā v24) and those who take experiences for the ultimate (v25–26).

equivalents.note: A feminine inner power in the central channel in both; frames and goals differ.

name: Illusory-body yoga
method_summary: Training to see oneself, the deity and the whole world as illusion, dream, mirror-image and painted Vajrasattva (Tilopa, from Nāgārjuna); in the Ārya completion stage, the arising of the self-consecration body of wind and mind after the empties, 'the vision of conventional truth', obtained by the guru's grace.

warnings.text: Without the self-consecration stage, obtained only by the guru's grace, labour in sūtra and tantra is in vain.

name: Dream yoga
method_summary: Recognizing the dream as dream and meditating on the profound meaning; focusing on nāda, bindu and the seed syllables of the five families, one sees buddha-fields and buddhas — 'the means of great bliss in sleep' (Tilopa, from Lavapa).

name: Clear-light yoga
method_summary: Summary: resting the mind in the central channel and steadying it in the drop at the heart, lights, rays, rainbows, dawn, sun and moon appear and fields become pure (Tilopa, from Nāgārjuna); in the Ārya scheme the fourth stage, full awakening in clear light.
signs_of_progress: the appearances listed by Tilopa (lights, rainbows, dawn, sun and moon, deities)

name: Intermediate-state yoga
method_summary: At death, recognizing the withdrawal of senses and elements and the gathering of winds at the heart, the yogin meditates deity yoga or rests in reality; when turning toward rebirth, meditates all appearance as the deity, thereby 'blocking' the intermediate state (Tilopa, from Sukhasiddhi).

name: Transference of consciousness (and entering another body)
method_summary: Summary only: at the time of death consciousness is sent upward with deity and seed syllable into the heart of the deity and guru, or into another body (Tilopa, from Sukhasiddhi). No method details recorded.

warnings.text: Taught only as oral instruction within the six dharmas; the text itself gives it to one prepared by the preceding yogas.

name: Karmamudrā (union with a consort)
method_summary: Summary only: sexual yoga with a qualified consort as a method of the higher consecrations and completion stage, to generate the gnosis of bliss and emptiness; the texts require consecration and pledges and warn against attachment. No procedure recorded.

warnings.text: The deluded who, attached to the bliss of union, call it the ultimate are like one who asks for news of Kāmarūpa at his own door.
The secret and wisdom consecrations are not to be taken by celibates; doing so destroys their vows and leads to bad destinies.
Tilopa: the gnosis arises only when there is no attachment (de la zhen med).

name: The six-branch yoga (ṣaḍaṅgayoga)
method_summary: Withdrawal (the senses resting in themselves), meditation (fivefold), breath control, retention, recollection and absorption; signs of dissolution (five in the Guhyasamāja, ten in the Kālacakra) lead to empty form and, in the Kālacakra, immutable bliss. Summary only for the breath and retention branches.
signs_of_progress: the five signs: mirage, smoke, fireflies, lamp, cloudless sky (GST 18)
the ten signs and the universal image (Sekoddeśa 26)
the fruits of each branch: blessing by mantras, five superknowledges, halo of light (GST 18.152–155)

warnings.text: Without the six-limbed service the supreme attainment does not arise; it is to be learned from the guru.

equivalents.note: The Maitrī Upaniṣad's six limbs (prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dhyāna, dhāraṇā, tarka, samādhi) share most names but not the order or the Buddhist signs and goal.

name: Resting in mahāmudrā (the Indian siddha instruction)
method_summary: Cutting the root of one's own mind and leaving awareness naked; letting the muddy water of concepts clear; neither blocking nor affirming appearances; relaxing body, speech and mind; mind without aim; looking at the sky-like nature until 'seeing' ceases; amanasikāra — not engaging concepts.

names.name: phyag rgya chen po / yid la mi byed pa

signs_of_progress: thoughts dissolve like clouds in space (v10)

warnings.text: For those of lesser intellect who cannot remain in the meaning, Tilopa prescribes working with the winds and gazes instead.
Arising intent obscures clear light; guarding vows conceptually degenerates the pledge.

name: Working with the winds (for those who cannot rest in the meaning)
method_summary: Summary only: Tilopa's 'holding the key points of wind' with gazes and methods of holding the mind for those of lesser capacity; in the tantras the drawing of winds into the central channel. No technique recorded.

warnings.text: Saraha criticizes forcing winds and head practices out of pride (King Dohā v22–24).

name: Devotion to the vajra master
method_summary: After mutual examination, the disciple regards the guru as inseparable from Vajradhara, bows three times a day, offers gifts, follows instructions and observes the etiquette of the Gurupañcāśikā (not stepping on his shadow, rising when he arrives, speaking softly); Saraha's songs praise the guru as boat, physician and sun.

warnings.text: The disciple who despises his master despises all buddhas and meets only suffering.

name: Examining the teacher (and the disciple)
method_summary: Before the bond teacher and disciple test each other; qualities to seek and faults to avoid are listed (Gurupañcāśikā 6–9).

warnings.text: A broken pledge is a fault for both teacher and disciple.

name: The tantric feast (gaṇacakra)
method_summary: Summary: a gathering of consecrated yogins and yoginīs with offerings, song (caryāgīti), dance and pledge substances, visualized as the maṇḍala. Details of substances not recorded.

warnings.text: Open only to those with consecration and pledges ('endowed with sign and pledge').

name: The observance (vratacaryā)
method_summary: Summary: after realization, the yogin wanders in cremation grounds and among outcastes wearing bone ornaments, acting 'mad', to test and deepen equal vision; a hidden observance (Pañcakrama 5.35).

warnings.text: One who has not realized should not engage in the conduct: it is like a kingdom seized by its subjects.
One who realizes the natural state but acts basely is like a king who comes down from his throne to sweep.

name: Tantric fire offering (homa)
method_summary: Offerings into the fire for the four activities (pacifying, increasing, subjugating, destroying) as part of sādhana and consecration rites (Vajrāvalī); the siddhas deride it when done without knowledge.

warnings.text: Pointless fire offerings only hurt the eyes with smoke.

name: Mantra recitation and approach retreat
method_summary: Recitation of the deity's mantra — spoken, whispered or mental, counted in the 'service' (sevā) phase — joined with the visualization of the deity.

name: Meditation on the syllable A
method_summary: Meditating on the letter A as the unborn gate of all dharmas (Mahāvairocana), the 'A' that is the foremost of letters (Nāmasaṃgīti).

name: Vajrasattva purification (the hundred-syllable mantra)
method_summary: Recitation of the hundred-syllable mantra of Vajrasattva with visualization, to purify faults and repair broken pledges.
notes: The mantra's occurrence in the Tattvasaṃgraha is recalled, not checked; the preliminary-practice use is chiefly documented in Tibetan sources.

name: Cheating death (mṛtyuvañcana)
method_summary: Summary only: reading omens of death and averting untimely death by Tārā practice (Vāgīśvarakīrti) or by drawing the life-wind into the central channel (Sekoddeśa). No technique recorded.

name: The body maṇḍala
method_summary: Meditating the deities and the twenty-four sites of the Heruka maṇḍala in the parts and channels of one's own body, associated especially with Ghaṇṭāpa's five-deity Cakrasaṃvara.
notes: The attribution of the body-maṇḍala system to Ghaṇṭāpa follows Tibetan presentations.

name: Pilgrimage to the sacred sites
method_summary: Walking to the twenty-four sites while reciting mantra (Jogipa, sent by Śavaripa per the lives); for the siddhas the body is itself the supreme site.

warnings.text: I have seen no holy place equal to the body.

name: Taking one's craft as the path (the siddhas' instruction)
method_summary: The guru turns the disciple's own trade or habit into the meditation: the weaver weaves phenomena into the dharmakāya, the cobbler tans the leather of concepts, the smith forges the three poisons in the fire of gnosis, the potter burns delusion in the kiln, the tailor stitches the three realms with compassion, the liar meditates all as a lie.

name: Purification of the dead (Sarvadurgatipariśodhana rites)
method_summary: Maṇḍala rites, fire offerings and consecration of the deceased's remains or effigy to free the dead from lower rebirths.
